findings.summary: The M3b rewrite fixed the link but not the referent. Line 62 reads "M3 adds compression, the filter and the ordinal registry", while roadmap.md:11 defines M2 as "Segment format ... key grammar with the adaptive filter" and roadmap.md:12 defines M3 as the ingest path (Helidon endpoint, bundling, flush). The segment-format work named on line 62 belongs to M2. This occurrence is also bare text, not a link, so contrary to the fix note only one of the two occurrences reads [M3](../../roadmap.md) and check-links.sh cannot see this one at all.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent decomposing M3 with the milestone skill reads M1/SPEC.md line 62 as the authority on what the segment format defers, and schedules compression, the adaptive filter and the ordinal registry into the ingest-path milestone. M2 then completes without the filter its own completion condition names, or the work is planned twice; ADR-0003's filter and the ordinal registry it makes mandatory land one milestone after the format that must encode them, which is a wire-format change after the golden files exist.

findings.summary: R1/R2 used as record labels in the head-of-line paragraph collides with the binding R<n> cost-rule namespace that cost.md:10 declares. Agreed as minor and carried forward, not fixed: local context ("R1 (durable)", "R2 (fast)") disambiguates for a human reader.
findings.failure_scenario: A grep-driven citation sweep for cost-rule references reports ADR-0013 as citing R1 and R2 (write coalescing, no LIST on hot paths) when it cites neither, sending a later cost audit to the wrong ADR.
